name: BMX Bandits
label: Creation Records
lede: Duglas T. Stewart named his Bellshill band thinking it would split in a week. Forty years on he's still the only constant, and half of Glasgow's guitar pop has passed through.

eras.title: Margarine tubs in Bellshill
eras.text: Duglas T. Stewart and Norman Blake started making songs together at school in Bellshill, a town outside Glasgow. Their first band, the Pretty Flowers, also had Sean Dickson and Frances McKee in it; within a few years those names would mean The Soup Dragons, Teenage Fanclub and The Vaselines.

q: Duglas would sing and I'd hit margarine tubs with kitchen utensils.
years.src: Wikipedia: BMX Bandits · Nicola Meighan: Interview: BMX Bandits · The Guardian: BMX Bandits'
years.h: The Pretty Flowers play wherever Bellshill lets them
years.p: Stewart's first band plays impromptu shows in parks, at schools and in the Hattonrigg Hotel.
years.xp:
Blake remembers the method: Stewart sang, and Blake banged on whatever was in the kitchen. The songs went down on a cassette player at Stewart's family home on Ramsey Wynd, where the name BMX Bandits was later dreamed up.

The Hattonrigg didn't always welcome them. "A group of punks decided to protest," Stewart told the Guardian, sitting outside like a picket line. Another night he and Blake played the Dead Kennedys' 'Nazi Punks Fuck Off' at a crowd of skinheads, and the police walked the band out the back.

years.src: Elefant Records: BMX Bandits · Wikipedia: BMX Bandits
years.h: Stephen Pastel tells Stewart to start a real band
years.p: Frances McKee leaves the Pretty Flowers to form [[The Vaselines|a70b63fd-cae7-4a5f-b338-b18343f3ee2f]] with [[Eugene Kelly|d1779852-7f21-4658-b1fe-fc300faf5a61]]. Stewart mails demos to [[Dan Treacy|ac345457-72fe-4c4e-8ace-2c3142d88ee4]] and Stephen Pastel, and Pastel's push turns the leftovers into BMX Bandits.
years.xp:
The name was picked in a hurry because Stewart didn't expect it to last. "I thought we'd split up in a week," he told Elefant.

Elefant lists the first core as Stewart, Blake, McKee, Dickson and drummer Hugh McLaughlin.

eras.title: The worst single of all time
eras.text: Pastel's 53rd & 3rd label put out the first records, Radio 1's Janice Long played them, and the music press hated them. Members came and went to form bands of their own, and Kurt Cobain, who was photographed in a BMX Bandits T-shirt, later said on New York radio that it was the one other band he'd join.

years.src: Nicola Meighan: Interview: BMX Bandits · Elefant Records: BMX Bandits · Wikipedia: BMX Bandits
years.h: Sounds reviews 'E102', the debut single on 53rd & 3rd
years.p: The Sounds reviewer found it "indigestably sickly sweet." Stewart loved the review and showed it to strangers.
years.xp:
Stewart wrote 'E102' with Sean Dickson; the title is the code for a food additive. A cover of 'What a Wonderful World' followed the same year.

Elefant quotes Stewart's view of rock: too many people dehumanise themselves in it.

years.cap: On stage at the Buzz Club, February 14, 1987
years.src: Elefant Records: BMX Bandits · Wikipedia: BMX Bandits
years.h: Sean Dickson leaves to concentrate on the Soup Dragons
years.p: Blake comes back with guitarist Gordon Keen and drummer [[Francis Macdonald|466340c2-f987-402f-a8af-cbec45fe15b7]]. Jim McCulloch follows Dickson to [[The Soup Dragons|5c42c9cf-5833-41d8-b600-177e70894046]].
years.xp: The 1986 line-up had included Dickson, McCulloch and Joe McAlinden. In 1990 Blake and Macdonald were in the first version of [[Teenage Fanclub|e6f8912b-7df9-4aae-b551-2cd03dc29588]], while staying in Stewart's orbit.

years.src: Wikipedia: BMX Bandits
yt: 'Fight for Your Right' on Full Scale Deflection
years.h: BMX Bandits do the Beastie Boys on BBC Scotland
years.p: On Full Scale Deflection, sharing the show with [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]], the band plays 'Fight for Your Right'. The Figure 4 EP comes out the same year.

years.src: Wikipedia: BMX Bandits
years.h: A Hattonrigg Hotel gig becomes Totally Groovy Live Experience!
years.p: The Bellshill hotel where the Pretty Flowers played is where the live album gets taped. Avalanche releases it.

years.src: Elefant Records: BMX Bandits · Wikipedia: BMX Bandits
years.h: The first studio album is called C86, after the NME tape
years.p: Click! releases it. The songs run from 'Right Across the Street' to the bossa nova of 'Rimbaud and Me'.

years.src: Elefant Records: BMX Bandits · Wikipedia: BMX Bandits
years.h: Eugene Kelly of the Vaselines sings on Star Wars
years.p: Vinyl Japan releases the band's tightest record yet, with 'Extraordinary' and 'Green Grow the Rushes'. A split single with [[Television Personalities|62c2cd94-30a8-43ed-9d06-8f689111c69c]] comes out on Clawfist.

eras.title: Creation, with Oasis in the support slot
eras.text: Alan McGee signed BMX Bandits to Creation Records on the strength of one song, 'Serious Drugs'. Within a year their new label-mates Oasis were opening for them.

years.src: The Guardian: BMX Bandits' · Tapete Records: BMX Bandits · Trouser Press: BMX Bandits · Wikipedia: BMX Bandits
years.h: 'Serious Drugs' gets BMX Bandits signed to Creation
years.p: Stewart's song about his own life is the first Creation release. Radio 1 staff told him they loved it, but it came out during the station's anti-drugs week and they couldn't play it.
years.xp:
The song came from a girlfriend suggesting he up his dose of antidepressants, Stewart told the Guardian in 2016. Of the Radio 1 timing he said: "That was hilarious."

Trouser Press called it "the best single of the band's career." It later turned up in the film This Year's Love, was covered by the Gigolo Aunts, and gave its name to Jim Burns's 2011 documentary about the band.

years.src: Tapete Records: BMX Bandits · Trouser Press: BMX Bandits
years.h: Life Goes On becomes their biggest seller
years.p: The Creation album, released in the US through TriStar, comes with the 'Little Hands' and 'Kylie's Got a Crush on Us' EPs.

years.cap: Keen, Stewart, Kelly, McAlinden and Macdonald in Tokyo
years.src: Oasis Recording Info: Gigography 1991-94 · The Influences: BMX Bandits · Wikipedia: BMX Bandits · Nicola Meighan: Interview: BMX Bandits
years.h: Oasis play their first UK tour dates opening for BMX Bandits
years.p: Stewart takes Creation's new signing on the road as a favour to Alan McGee. Oasis open at Keele University, then Sheffield University and the Wherehouse in Derby.

years.src: Elefant Records: BMX Bandits · Trouser Press: BMX Bandits
years.h: Gettin' Dirty is made by a settled line-up
years.p: Francis Macdonald writes alongside Stewart, with Finlay Macdonald, John Hogarty and ex-Soup Dragon Sushil K. Dade in the band.
years.xp: Elefant calls this the first time BMX Bandits worked as a stable band rather than a rotating cast. Trouser Press preferred the earlier records and thought the sound had been "smoothed down and gussied up."

years.src: Elefant Records: BMX Bandits · Wikipedia: BMX Bandits · Wikipedia: Duglas T. Stewart
years.h: Theme Park is the last Creation album
years.p: Stewart also makes Duglas Stewart's Frankenstein, a solo album with Bandits on it, for Vinyl Japan.
years.xp: Elefant says Kim Fowley came to Glasgow and wrote songs with the band. An album credited to BMX Bandits with Fowley, Hidden Agenda, came out on Receiver in 1997; Wikipedia says the group didn't authorise it.

eras.title: Without Macdonald, with a documentary
eras.text: After the Creation years the band moved between small labels before settling at Spain's Elefant Records. Stewart's twenty-year partnership with Macdonald ended, new singers came in, and Glasgow got a film about the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: BMX Bandits
years.h: Down at the Hop comes out on Shoeshine
years.p: The first BMX Bandits album in seven years comes out on the Shoeshine label.

years.src: Wikipedia: BMX Bandits
years.h: Stewart and Francis Macdonald stop writing together
years.p: The partnership that had run since 1987 ends, though Macdonald still plays on later records.

years.src: Wikipedia: BMX Bandits · Tapete Records: BMX Bandits
years.h: Rachel Allison sings half of Bee Stings
years.p: Allison and the Pearlfishers' David Scott joined for 2006's My Chain, Stewart's own favourite. On the Poppydisc follow-up, Allison co-writes 'Our Secret Life' with Norman Blake.

years.src: Wikipedia: BMX Bandits · Nicola Meighan: Interview: BMX Bandits
years.h: Serious Drugs, the BMX Bandits film, premieres at Glasgow Popfest
years.p: Jim Burns's documentary opens at the Glasgow Film Theatre.

years.src: Elefant Records: BMX Bandits · Wikipedia: BMX Bandits · The Guardian: BMX Bandits'
years.h: Dickson and McCulloch come back for BMX Bandits in Space
years.p: A concept album for Elefant about a traveller crossing time and space looking for forgiveness and home. Chloe Philip of TeenCanteen joins the next year.
years.xp: It was the band's best seller since the Creation years, the Guardian reported in 2016.

eras.title: Forty years and a masterpiece
eras.text: Stewart kept going with Stuart Kidd, Chloe Philip and producer Andrew Pattie, and moved to Germany's Tapete. The late records drew the best reviews the band ever had.

years.cap: Anton Newcombe and Duglas T. Stewart, 2017
years.src: Wikipedia: BMX Bandits
years.h: Anton Newcombe turns up on BMX Bandits Forever
years.p: The tenth studio album, on Elefant, has the Brian Jonestown Massacre leader on it. The band also appears in the documentary Teenage Superstars.

q: Against the odds, BMX Bandits have finally painted their masterpiece.
years.src: Wikipedia: BMX Bandits · Tapete Records: BMX Bandits
years.h: Dreamers on the Run gets the band's best reviews in decades
years.p: Stewart and Andrew Pattie produce, with Pattie's string arrangements. Uncut called it "a bold and seductive exploration of symphonic pop."
years.xp: Stewart and Pattie had already scored the film Dreaded Light together for Tapete in 2023. Tapete calls Dreamers on the Run the band's most acclaimed record.

years.src: Tapete Records: BMX Bandits
years.h: 15 Big Ones marks forty years
years.p: Tapete's best-of mixes the hits with songs Stewart thinks should have been singles.
years.xp: Stewart, to Tapete: "Almost everything wonderful that has happened in my adult life has come out of me being in BMX Bandits."

sources.title: The Guardian: BMX Bandits' Duglas T Stewart (Peter Ross, 2016)
